The retention rate formula depends on whether you are measuring **customer retention** or **employee retention**.

### Customer Retention Rate Formula

The customer retention rate measures the percentage of existing customers a business keeps over a given time period.[[1]](https://www.gainsight.com/blog/how-to-calculate-customer-retention-rate/)

- **Formula:**   
Customer Retention Rate=(Ending Customers−New Customers Starting Customers)×100 Customer Retention Rate equals open paren the fraction with numerator Ending Customers minus New Customers and denominator Starting Customers end-fraction close paren cross 100 C u s t o m e r R e t e n t i o n R a t e=E n d i n g C u s t o m e r s−N e w C u s t o m e r s S t a r t i n g C u s t o m e r s×1 0 0
- **Where:** 
	- **Ending Customers:** Total number of customers at the end of the period
	- **New Customers:** Number of new customers acquired during the period
	- **Starting Customers:** Total number of customers at the start of the period[[1]](https://www.gainsight.com/blog/how-to-calculate-customer-retention-rate/)

You can read more about tracking customer metrics through platforms like [Zendesk](https://www.zendesk.com/blog/customer-experience/retention/calculate-customer-retention-rate/) or [Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/service/digital-customer-engagement-platform/customer-retention-rate/).[[1]](https://www.salesforce.com/service/digital-customer-engagement-platform/customer-retention-rate/)[[2]](https://www.zendesk.com/blog/customer-experience/retention/calculate-customer-retention-rate/)
---

### Employee Retention Rate Formula
The employee retention rate measures the percentage of employees who stay with an organization over a specific timeframe (excluding new hires made during that period).[[1]](https://vendordirectory.shrm.org/company/911224/news/3557390/how-to-calculate-employee-retention-rate-in-2025)[[2]](https://www.cultureamp.com/blog/how-to-calculate-employee-retention-rate)

- **Formula:**   
Employee Retention Rate=(Number of Employees at End of Period−Number of New Hires Number of Employees at Start of Period)×100 Employee Retention Rate equals open paren the fraction with numerator Number of Employees at End of Period minus Number of New Hires and denominator Number of Employees at Start of Period end-fraction close paren cross 100 E m p l o y e e R e t e n t i o n R a t e=N u m b e r o f E m p l o y e e s a t E n d o f P e r i o d−N u m b e r o f N e w H i r e s N u m b e r o f E m p l o y e e s a t S t a r t o f P e r i o d×1 0 0
- **Where:** 
	- **Start of Period:** Total workforce headcount at the beginning of the timeframe
	- **End of Period:** Total workforce headcount at the end of the timeframe
	- **New Hires:** Employees added during the timeframe (which are subtracted so they do not skew the original team's retention)[[1]](https://www.cultureamp.com/blog/how-to-calculate-employee-retention-rate)[[2]](https://vendordirectory.shrm.org/company/911224/news/3557390/how-to-calculate-employee-retention-rate-in-2025)

Guidance on tracking workforce metrics is available via resources like [ADP](https://www.adp.com/resources/articles-and-insights/articles/r/retention-rate.aspx).[[1]](https://www.adp.com/resources/articles-and-insights/articles/r/retention-rate.aspx)Are you looking to calculate **customer retention** or **employee retention** , and what **time period** (such as monthly or annually) are you analyzing?
